page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7a.16xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated physical cores utilizing the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7T83 processor running at a clock speed of 2.55 GHz. The instance is equipped with 512.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 16 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng and Passmark CPU scores placing in the top 25%. Memory performance is mixed; while small-block cached read bandwidth is highly competitive, large-block uncached read and write bandwidths fall into the average range. The instance also demonstrates strong capabilities in cryptographic operations, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and small-model LLM inference, while database operations and static web serving throughput remain average.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.r7a.16xlarge offers high resource density for memory-bound applications, allowing consolidation of large datasets in RAM. However, the lack of bundled local storage represents a key tradeoff, requiring reliance on external network-attached storage which may impact overall I/O latency.

This instance is suited for memory-intensive workloads such as in-memory databases, large-scale caching layers, data analytics, and medium-scale language model inference. The dedicated CPU allocation and high memory capacity also make it appropriate for enterprise applications requiring consistent compute performance without virtualization overhead.
